name: ESP32-C3
description: Espressif ESP32-C3: a 32-bit RISC-V core (RV32IMC, ESP-RV) at up to 160 MHz, 400 KiB of SRAM, 384 KiB of ROM, external SPI flash behind an instruction and data cache, Wi-Fi and Bluetooth LE; the ESP32-C3-DevKitM-1's MCU. In progress (the RTOS boards plan, part 2): the core and its interrupt controller first.

memory.name: rom

functional.claims: Work in progress (the RTOS boards plan, part 2, steps 1 and 2). The ESP-RV core: RV32IMC with user mode and the ESP32-C3's own CSRs (TRM chapter 1): mstatus's MIE, MPIE, MPP and TW, a vectored mtvec, five-bit mcause codes, the performance counter (mpcer, mpcmr, mpccr) and the user-mode one the ROM uses, the trigger module's eight triggers (exact and NAPOT match on execute, load and store, tcontrol), 16 PMP entries without static priority, and the cpu_gpio CSRs. The interrupt matrix and controller: 62 sources mapped onto CPU interrupts 1-31, level and edge types, priorities 1-15, the threshold, the 4-cycle latency, the clear toggle. The boot: Espressif's own boot ROM (esp32c3_rev3_rom.elf, chip revision v0.3) runs from the reset vector, reads the strapping pins (GPIO_STRAP), reports the reset cause (RTC_CNTL), loads an ESP image's segments from the flash through SPI1, checks its checksum and SHA-256 on the SHA accelerator and jumps to it. The in-package 4 MB flash, an XMC XM25QH32C as its datasheet has it (its instructions, status registers, busy times, security registers and power-down), behind SPI0 and SPI1; the cache and MMU mapping its 64 KB pages on the instruction and data buses. UART0 and UART1 (FIFOs, frames at the baud rate, interrupts); RTC_CNTL's reset causes, RTC timer, RTC watchdog with its flash-boot protection and the software resets; the Debug Assistant's PC logging (the ROM's Saved PC). Every register of Espressif's SVD with its reset value.
omissions: the clocks (SYSTEM, the PLL), SYSTIMER, the timer groups and their watchdogs (TIMG0's flash-boot watchdog does not run), the GPIO matrix and IO MUX, USB Serial/JTAG, the eFuse controller and every other peripheral (in progress)
the cache's enable and bus-shut bits, the MMU entry fault and the access counters; the cache holds whole pages, not 16 KB of lines (core/mcu/esp32c3/cache.c)
the flash's QPI mode, continuous read mode, SFDP table and block protection; SPI_MEM's auto-suspend and wait-idle, and the SPI clock's time (transfers take none)
the SHA accelerator's DMA mode and its block time
the debug module and the debug CSRs
the performance counter's load and jump hazard events
the interrupt controller's transient state after a register write

timed.claims: Instruction timing estimated from the RISC-V core's per-class cost table, not the ESP-RV pipeline's.
omissions: the SPI flash transfers' time (the flash's own program and erase times are counted)

electrical.claims: GPIO pin-model defaults at 3.3 V from the datasheet's DC characteristics (table 5-4): VIH 0.75 VDD, VIL 0.25 VDD, VOH 0.8 VDD, VOL 0.1 VDD, 45 kOhm pulls, 40 mA source and 28 mA sink at the strongest drive.
omissions: the RTC and SPI pads' own supplies
